queries: GET http://ctdbase.org/ ; GET https://www.ctdbase.org/ ; GET https://ctd.mdibl.org/  (alternate-host probes)
resources.barrier_detail: Every CTD path tested — the documented batchQuery.go programmatic endpoint (GET and POST), basicQuery.go, detail.go, /downloads/ and even /robots.txt — returns HTTP 302 with an identical 2774-byte HTML interstitial (Server: nginx/1.30.4, Content-Type: text/html, title 'Comparative Toxicogenomic Database'). The interstitial loads https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/altcha-org/altcha/dist/altcha.min.js, renders <altcha-widget challengeurl="/captcha.go?altcha=yes"> inside <form method="post" action="/captcha.go">, and states verbatim: 'To continue, we need to verify you are a human.  If you are having trouble accessing computationally from any device, please use a browser to access CTD from that device and complete the captcha verification.' No Location header and no TSV/JSON is ever returned; the 302 is served to the same URL. Browser-like User-Agent (Chrome/129 UA string) made no difference (still 302 / 2774 bytes / 4 'altcha' occurrences). Alternate hosts: http://ctdbase.org/ -> 301 to https (then same gate); https://www.ctdbase.org/ -> curl 60, 'SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name' (no such vhost); https://ctd.mdibl.org/ -> curl 60, 'unable to get local issuer certificate' (legacy host, not a usable mirror). This is a deliberate anti-automation human-verification gate, not a paywall or a login. I did not attempt to solve the ALTCHA proof-of-work, because the site explicitly declares automated access out of scope and asks for a human in a browser.
resources.notes: ZERO CTD content was retrieved, so no CTD claim in this sweep is evidence-backed. Had the gate been open, the intended queries were (a) chemical->disease curated/inferred associations for the priority oligonucleotides, and (b) the reverse query disease MESH:D013921 (Thrombocytopenia) -> chemicals, to see whether any oligonucleotide therapeutic is a CTD curated chemical at all. Note for the record that CTD's value here would in any case be bibliographic (curated chemical-disease assertions extracted from literature) rather than primary per-donor platelet measurements, so it would rank low against the Phase 2 human-in-vitro priority even if reachable. A human operator can clear the captcha once in a browser and then re-run the batchQuery URLs above in the same session.

resources.barrier_detail: No access barrier for the REST API. Two incidental non-blocking notes: (1) the ICE web UI is a Vaadin single-page app — every HTML path (/, /DATASETDESCRIPTION, /Tools, /ICEData, /api/datasets, /rest/search) returns HTTP 200 with the same ~2135-byte app shell, so the UI is not scrapable and the REST API is the only programmatic route; (2) the REST API rate-limits, HTTP 429 with an empty reason phrase on back-to-back POSTs — cleared on retry after ~25 s, all queries above eventually completed with HTTP 200.
resources.notes: EVIDENCED NULL, with the detail that makes it an evidenced null rather than a vague one. (a) ICE's own enumerated assay vocabulary is 381 names; filtering it for haemostasis terms yields exactly six: 'Hematology', 'Clinical Chemistry' (adjacent), 'Regulation of Blood Coagulation', 'AcuteTox - Regulation of Blood Coagulation' (+MOA variant), 'CardioTox - Endothelial Injury/Coagulation' (+MOA variant). There is no platelet-count, platelet-activation, platelet-aggregation or megakaryocyte assay name in ICE at all. (b) The 34-DTXSID oligonucleotide POST returned HTTP 200 with exactly ONE record in the entire response (506 bytes): mipomersen DTXSID10142864, assay 'httk, Human Plasma Fraction Unbound', endpoint Fu = 0.05 unitless, species Human, reference 'httk2.3.1, Lombardo 2018'. That is an in-silico QSAR-predicted plasma protein binding value, not a measurement, and it is unrelated to platelets. Every other oligonucleotide therapeutic in ICE has zero records of any kind. (c) The same oligonucleotide set restricted to the five haemostasis assays returned the API usage/help block, i.e. 'CASRN not found or no results found' — zero rows. (d) The positive control (one chemid + assay 'Hematology') returned HTTP 200 / 12,417,375 bytes / 25,167 records, proving the channel works; note the API returns the whole assay slice rather than filtering to the submitted chemid, so this is effectively the full ICE Hematology content. Within it: 544 distinct substances, 25 distinct endpoints, species distribution Rat 16402 / Rabbit 7524 / Mouse 1205 / Hamster 30 / Dog 6 and HUMAN ZERO, and exactly ONE record whose endpoint is 'Platelet (decreased)'. Zero of the 544 substances is an oligonucleotide (regex /sen$|siran$|mersen|oligo|antisense|nucleot/ over substance names: no match). ICE's haematology content is ToxRefDB-sourced animal in vivo guideline-study findings, so even setting the oligonucleotide absence aside it cannot serve the Phase 2 human-in-vitro / in-vitro-to-animal-extrapolation priority. ICE is therefore effectively NOT APPLICABLE to this endpoint, and I am reporting that with the query evidence above rather than as a bare null. Bulk downloads were inventoried and confirm the same scope: /downloads/DataonNICE/ holds ADME_Parameters.xlsx, Acute_{Dermal,Inhalation,Oral}_Toxicity.xlsx, Cancer.xlsx, DART.xlsx, Endocrine.xlsx, Exposure_Predictions.xlsx, Eye_Irritation.xlsx, Skin_{Irritation_Corrosion,Sensitization}.xlsx, ChemicalTaxonomies.zip and the cHTS ToxCast mirrors cHTS2019_invitrodb3 / cHTS2019_invitrodb32 / cHTS2021_invitrodb33 / cHTS2022_invitrodb34 / cHTS2023_invitrodb35 — no haematology or platelet dataset is published there at all. ICE-REST API examples PDF retrieved OK (HTTP 200, 1,654,684 bytes) and confirms CASRN/DTXSID/InChIKey/SMILES are the only accepted chemical identifiers; chemical NAMES are not queryable, which is why DTXSIDs were resolved first (see the CompTox note in the ToxCast row).

resources.barrier_detail:
Two genuine blocks, neither of which prevented the substantive answer because the authoritative bulk files were reachable. (1) CCTE REST API api-ccte.epa.gov is unreachable from this environment: 'curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502', HTTP 000, zero bytes, on every attempt; the agent egress proxy's own status endpoint logs it as kind 'connect_rejected', detail 'gateway answered 502 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', host 'api-ccte.epa.gov:443' at 2026-10-03T01:09:44Z. This is an egress-policy denial at the proxy, not an EPA outage, and no API key was involved. (2) The CompTox dashboard's bioactivity microservice is down server-side: GET /dashboard-api/bioactivity/summary/search/by-dtxsid/DTXSID60172611 and /dashboard-api/bioactivity/data/search/by-dtxsid/DTXSID60172611 both return HTTP 503 with body '

503 Service Unavailable

No server is available to handle this request.' Other dashboard-api routes are fine (ccdapp1 chemical search HTTP 200), and sibling guesses return clean HTTP 404 JSON ('No static resource ...'), so 503 is specific to the bioactivity service. Also recorded for completeness: ccdapp2/chemical-detail/search/by-dtxsid/DTXSID60172611 returns HTTP 202 with an empty array '[ ]' rather than a chemical record. One transient, resolved on retry: first fetch of the EPA page gave 'curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL', succeeded on the next attempt (HTTP 200, 82251 bytes).
resources.notes: ANSWERS THE FAMILY QUESTION DIRECTLY AND WITH EVIDENCE. (A) Does ToxCast have a thrombocytopenia/platelet endpoint? NO. Across all 1647 per-assay-endpoint documentation files in the current invitroDB v4.2 package, only 8 filenames match any haemostasis term, and all 8 are BioSeek/BioMAP vascular-inflammation readouts, not platelet assays: AEID146_BSK_3C_Eselectin, AEID162_BSK_3C_Thrombomodulin, AEID176_BSK_4H_Pselectin, AEID228_BSK_CASM3C_Thrombomodulin, AEID280_BSK_LPS_Eselectin, AEID306_BSK_SAg_Eselectin, AEID2917_BSK_IMphg_ESelectin, AEID2933_BSK_LPS_Thrombomodulin. The Assay Target Mappings workbook confirms the only haemostasis-adjacent gene targets in the whole battery are SELP (selectin P), selectin E, thrombomodulin and 'platelet activating factor receptor'. There is no platelet count, no platelet aggregation, no platelet activation, no PAC-1, no GPVI/GP6, no ITGA2B/CD41, no PF4, no thrombopoietin/MPL and no megakaryocyte endpoint anywhere in invitroDB v4.2. BSK_4H_Pselectin is a P-selectin ELISA in the BioMAP 4H human primary-cell system (human endothelial cells), i.e. an endothelial activation marker, NOT a platelet-derived P-selectin readout, and must not be mistaken for one. (B) Does ToxCast use human platelet material at all? Only as a protein source for cell-free receptor-binding assays, per the annotation text: NVS_GPCR_hTXA2 'uses extracted gene-proteins from Human platelets in a cell-free assay' (thromboxane A2 receptor), NVS_GPCR_hV1A (same, vasopressin V1A), NVS_TR_hSERT 'uses extracted gene-proteins from Human platelet membranes', plus NVS_GPCR_rabPAF from rabbit platelets. These are radioligand-binding assays on platelet membrane preparations; they report no platelet function, count or activation outcome and so do not constitute human in vitro platelet toxicity data. (C) Is any oligonucleotide in ToxCast? NO. The ToxCast tested-chemical inventory was checked directly: the Cytotoxicity Burst Output workbook lists 10,487 distinct DTXSIDs and the Analytical QC workbook 8,843; the intersection with the 34 oligonucleotide-therapeutic DTXSIDs is EMPTY in both. No 'oligonucleotide', 'antisense', 'siRNA' or 'aptamer' chemical name appears in either file. The only 'phosphorothioate' strings in the entire package are organophosphate-pesticide QC comments (e.g. 'The phosphorothioate functional group has been hydrolyzed. Chlorpyrifos is unstable to hydrolysis...'), confirming that in ToxCast 'phosphorothioate' means an OP insecticide moiety, not an oligonucleotide backbone — a false-friend worth flagging for any future automated search of this family. (D) DSSTox DOES mint identifiers for oligonucleotide drugs even though ToxCast never tested them, and these are worth keeping for cross-referencing: oblimersen sodium DTXSID60172611, drisapersen DTXSID001508132, aprinocarsen DTXSID201416303 (sodium DTXSID90186786), alicaforsen DTXSID701030532 (sodium DTXSID501425567), mipomersen DTXSID10142864 (sodium DTXSID20212108), nusinersen sodium DTXSID301027785, inotersen DTXSID501027905, fomivirsen DTXSID501027529, eteplirsen DTXSID701027882, golodirsen DTXSID401027895, viltolarsen DTXSID501508470, casimersen DTXSID201508776, volanesorsen DTXSID801337064, custirsen DTXSID401425564, apatorsen DTXSID20143044, trabedersen DTXSID701053940, imetelstat sodium DTXSID001424340, pegaptanib sodium DTXSID40944934, defibrotide sodium DTXSID301027878, inclisiran DTXSID501509666, patisiran DTXSID301027892, givosiran DTXSID701027901, lumasiran DTXSID401508641, vutrisiran DTXSID301509658, fitusiran DTXSID201508302. Six priority agents have NO DSSTox record at all (empty result arrays): donidalorsen, pelacarsen, olezarsen, tofersen, nedosiran, avacincaptad. Research-code synonyms are not indexed either: 'ISIS 3521', 'ISIS 5132', 'ISIS 2302', 'G3139' and 'GSK2402968' all returned empty, so DSSTox/CompTox cannot be used to resolve oligonucleotide research codes to INN names.

candidates.endpoint_gap_it_closes: NONE for oligonucleotide-induced thrombocytopenia. It contains zero oligonucleotide chemicals and zero platelet-count/activation endpoints. Its only two legitimate uses are (i) citable proof that ToxCast/Tox21 provides no coverage of this endpoint or this chemical class, so the tox-database family can be closed out with evidence rather than an unexplained null, and (ii) a documented precedent that human platelet membrane preparations (NVS_GPCR_hTXA2, NVS_GPCR_hV1A, NVS_TR_hSERT) and a human primary-cell P-selectin ELISA (BSK_4H_Pselectin, AEID176, target SELP) are already established, publicly annotated HTS formats — relevant if the challenge submission needs to justify a human in vitro platelet assay design against existing regulatory-grade precedent.
candidates.expected_usable_observations: 0 oligonucleotide-platelet observations. 1647 assay-endpoint annotation records and ~10,487 tested-chemical DTXSIDs of context/negative-coverage metadata.

notes: FAMILY VERDICT: this family yields NO usable evidence for oligonucleotide-induced thrombocytopenia, and the honest headline is that the tox_databases family can be closed. Two of the three resources were genuinely searched and returned evidenced nulls; the third (CTD) was not searched at all because it is behind a hard anti-automation gate. BOTTOM LINE PER RESOURCE. CTD: zero content retrieved; every endpoint including the documented batchQuery.go API and the bulk /downloads/ directory returns HTTP 302 to an ALTCHA human-verification interstitial that states in plain text that computational access should be replaced by a browser session. Recorded as technical_block, searched=false. Nothing about CTD in this file is an evidence-backed null. ICE: searched successfully via the REST API. Its assay vocabulary (381 names, enumerated by the API itself) contains no platelet or megakaryocyte assay; its entire Hematology slice is 25,167 ToxRefDB animal in vivo records across 544 substances with species Rat/Rabbit/Mouse/Hamster/Dog and HUMAN=0, containing exactly one 'Platelet (decreased)' record and zero oligonucleotides; the 34-DTXSID oligonucleotide query returns exactly one row in total, a QSAR-PREDICTED mipomersen plasma free fraction (Fu=0.05, httk2.3.1 / Lombardo 2018) that is not a measurement and not platelet-related. ICE is effectively not applicable to this endpoint and is reported as such with the queries that prove it. TOXCAST: searched successfully via the authoritative invitroDB v4.2 bulk summary files. No platelet-count, platelet-aggregation, platelet-activation, PAC-1, P-selectin-on-platelets, GPVI, PF4, CD41/ITGA2B, thrombopoietin/MPL or megakaryocyte endpoint exists among its 1647 assay endpoints; the only haemostasis-adjacent targets are SELP, selectin E, thrombomodulin and PAF receptor, all in BioMAP human ENDOTHELIAL/vascular co-culture assays. Human platelet material appears only as membrane protein preparations for cell-free radioligand binding (NVS_GPCR_hTXA2, NVS_GPCR_hV1A, NVS_TR_hSERT), which report receptor binding, not platelet toxicity. The ToxCast tested-chemical inventory (10,487 DTXSIDs in the cytotoxicity-burst file, 8,843 in analytical QC) contains NONE of the 34 oligonucleotide DTXSIDs. The guidance's hypothesis that these resources are small-molecule-centric and that oligonucleotides are genuinely absent is therefore CONFIRMED with primary-file evidence, not asserted. TWO REUSABLE BY-PRODUCTS worth carrying into other sweeps. (1) A DSSTox identifier crosswalk for 28 oligonucleotide therapeutics (listed in the ToxCast row's notes), which is useful for joining to any EPA/NIEHS-derived resource even though none of them has bioactivity data. Six priority agents have no DSSTox record at all: donidalorsen, pelacarsen, olezarsen, tofersen, nedosiran, avacincaptad; and the research codes ISIS 3521, ISIS 5132, ISIS 2302, G3139 and GSK2402968 are not indexed as synonyms, so CompTox cannot resolve oligonucleotide research codes. (2) A FALSE-FRIEND WARNING: in ToxCast and in chemical-tox databases generally, 'phosphorothioate' denotes the organophosphate-pesticide moiety (chlorpyrifos, etrimfos, chlorpyrifos-methyl), not an oligonucleotide backbone. Any automated keyword sweep of chemical-toxicology resources on 'phosphorothioate + platelet' will be dominated by OP-insecticide chemistry and must be filtered on chemical class. CONSTRAINTS OBSERVED: no accounts created, no credentials supplied, nothing purchased, no authors contacted, and the CTD ALTCHA proof-of-work was deliberately not solved. No NCT numbers, PMIDs or DOIs are asserted in this file except ones actually returned by a service (figshare DOI 10.23645/epacomptox.6328037.v12 from the figshare API; the invitroDB record DOI 10.23645/epacomptox.6062623 as linked from the EPA page). No clinical-trial identifiers were found in this family, so nothing required ClinicalTrials.gov verification.
